title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din was a Kurdish sultan of Egypt/Syria active c.1169-1193, a century later and 3,000 km away from Zaragoza's rivals or Valencia in 1081-1094. The dialogue calls the enemy 'Rival Raider Chief' and 'Governor of Valencia', so the hero unit directly contradicts the text; a generic Mameluke/Cavalry Archer or a scripted named King would have been available.

One enemy player serves as both the 'rival raiders' of the Ebro valley and the city of Valencia, so El Cid's actual opponents at Almenar/Tevar (Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona and al-Hayib of Lerida, i.e. partly Christian Catalan forces) are collapsed into a single Saracen-style Muslim army.

CAMEL_RIDER x3 in an Iberian setting: camel cavalry was essentially absent from Andalusi and Taifa field armies; light javelin cavalry (jinetes) would be the regional norm, and the engine's Light Cavalry/Cavalry Archer units cover this better.

Al-Mu'tamin of Zaragoza, El Cid's actual employer and the pivot of the whole 1081-1086 period, exists only as a text line with no allied player or units, so the 'mercenary in Muslim service' premise is never enacted on the map.

issues_found: SALADIN is placed as the enemy leader standing in for both the 'Rival Raider Chief' and the 'Governor of Valencia'. Saladin is an Ayyubid ruler of Egypt/Syria a century later (d. 1193) and utterly unconnected to al-Andalus; a renamed generic Camel Rider, Mameluke or Champion would have been the correct, entirely avoidable substitution.

Both players' civilizations are left RANDOM, so architecture sets, unit rosters and tech could render Valencia as, e.g., Britons or Mongols; Spanish/Saracen (or Berber) assignment was available and free.

Al-Mu'tamin of Zaragoza speaks as El Cid's patron but exists only as text - there is no Zaragozan player, no allied Muslim army, and thus no representation of El Cid serving a Taifa king, the central fact of the exile years.

The same Player 2 hosts both the northern 'rival raider camp' and Valencia, so the historically distinct campaigns (against Aragon/Berenguer Ramon II in the Ebro, then the Levantine conquest) are collapsed into one enemy.

Valencia is reduced to a wall-and-castle assault decided by killing a hero; the historical capture was a twenty-month blockade and starvation siege ending in negotiated surrender after Ibn Jahhaf's coup - nothing in the triggers models attrition or blockade.
The 'rival raider camp' is an invented generic objective; El Cid's Zaragozan service produced named victories (Almenar 1082, Morella/Olocau 1084) that could have been referenced.
Enemy force of 9 Cavalry Archers plus Camel Riders is a steppe-style composition; Andalusi/Almoravid armies would be better rendered with light cavalry, spearmen and archers on foot.

SALADIN is placed as the enemy hero standing for the Governor of Valencia (and apparently also the Zaragozan rivals): Saladin was a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan active c. 1169-1193 in Egypt/Syria, an unrelated culture roughly a century after 1094. A renamed generic unit (e.g. a Camel Rider, Sultan, or King) or an Andalusi-flavoured stand-in was available and would have been correct.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit lines and tech are unassigned; Spanish for El Cid's retinue and Saracens for Zaragoza/Valencia were obvious available choices for Iberia c. 1081-1094.
A single enemy player (Player 2) doubles as al-Mu'tamin's northern rivals AND the defenders of Valencia, collapsing two distinct, chronologically separated opponents into one force with one hero.

Valencia is represented only by a Castle, two Guard Towers and a stone wall line with 9 Cavalry Archers and 3 Camel Riders; the historical fall of Valencia was a nearly two-year blockade and starvation siege, not a mobile cavalry-archer defence, and no siege/starvation mechanic or timer represents that.
The 'rival raider camp' is an invented generic objective in place of the documented engagements of the Zaragoza service (Almenar 1082, Morella, the defeat of al-Mundhir and the Count of Barcelona).
TREE_PALM_FOREST across the map is a stylistic gesture toward the Mediterranean but reads as North African/desert rather than the Ebro valley terrain the narration places the first battle in.
